checks.s: The proposed aggregate pool, including the initial reserve and the 325,000-share rollover, is between 1,920,000 and 2,200,000 shares (12%–13.75% of 16,000,000 fully diluted shares).
The compromise includes the 325,000-share rollover accepted by both sides.
The deliverable identifies the Aldridge Lydon market median of 12% as an anchor for the compromise pool size.
The deliverable calculates each side’s dollar-value concession from its original position using the $12.00 implied per-share price and shows the concessions are roughly balanced.
The deliverable identifies the investor’s proposed pool as 2,400,000 shares, or 15% of 16,000,000 fully diluted shares.
The deliverable identifies the founders’ proposed new pool as 1,280,000 shares, or 8% of 16,000,000 fully diluted shares.
The deliverable cites the Aldridge Lydon market study’s median Series C option pool of 12% (range 10%–15%) for late-stage life sciences companies to support the compromise position.
The compromise includes a mechanism to roll 325,000 unallocated 2020 Plan shares into the 2025 Plan.
The rollover and recycling mechanism, including future forfeitures and cancellations flowing back into the pool, is capped at a stated number of shares.
The compromise states an aggregate cap of no more than 2,400,000 shares issuable under the 2025 Plan, including the initial reserve, rollover, and evergreen accrual, without stockholder approval.
The compromise includes an automatic annual evergreen increase with a defined per-year share cap.
The evergreen provision includes a cap expressed as a percentage of shares outstanding, such as shares outstanding on January 1 of each year.
The evergreen provision states a sunset period after which automatic increases cease.
The evergreen provision expressly allows the Board to add fewer than the maximum number of shares or no shares in a given year.
The Change of Control provision grants 100% single-trigger acceleration to Dr. Chandrasekaran (CEO), Sorokin (CTO), and Dr. Osei (CSO).
The single-trigger acceleration for Dr. Chandrasekaran, Sorokin, and Dr. Osei is not conditioned on a Qualifying Termination.
The Change of Control provision does not grant single-trigger acceleration to all option holders and places at least rank-and-file employees on a different, double-trigger regime.
The Change of Control provision includes at least two participant tiers with different acceleration treatment.
Tier 2 participants (VP-level and above, excluding Tier 1 founders) receive partial immediate acceleration upon a Change of Control.
The remaining Tier 2 unvested shares accelerate only upon a Qualifying Termination within a defined post-Change-of-Control period.
Tier 3 rank-and-file employees receive Change of Control acceleration only upon a Qualifying Termination within a post-Change-of-Control period.
The compromise defines Qualifying Termination to include termination without Cause and resignation for Good Reason.
The Good Reason definition includes a material compensation reduction with a stated percentage threshold.
The Good Reason definition includes a material diminution of role or responsibilities.
The Good Reason definition includes relocation beyond a specified mileage.
The Good Reason definition includes a material breach by the Company.
The Good Reason definition specifies a period for the holder to notify the Company.
The Good Reason definition specifies a period for the Company to cure the condition.
The PTEP provision sets a distinct exercise period for voluntary resignation.
The PTEP provision sets a distinct exercise period for involuntary termination without Cause.
The PTEP provision sets a distinct exercise period for death or disability.
The PTEP provision sets a distinct exercise period for termination for Cause.
The PTEP for involuntary termination without Cause is longer than the PTEP for voluntary resignation.
Each PTEP for a non-Cause termination category—voluntary resignation, involuntary termination without Cause, and death or disability—is at least 120 days.
The PTEP provision gives voluntary resignations a longer exercise period based on a stated service-tenure threshold.
The PTEP provision limits the exercise period to 3 months after termination to the extent necessary to preserve ISO status under IRC § 422, or 12 months for Disability.
The PTEP provision allows the holder to elect NSO treatment to access the extended exercise period.
The PTEP provision includes a Section 409A savings clause or other stated Section 409A-compliant limitation on an extended exercise period.
The compromise retains a repurchase right for vested shares following termination for Cause.
The repurchase exercise window is no longer than 120 days.
The repurchase right automatically sunsets upon an IPO, a Change of Control, or a stated anniversary date.
The repurchase price for non-Cause terminations is Fair Market Value.
The repurchase price for a Cause termination is at least the original exercise price paid by the holder.
The deliverable identifies the investor’s original lower-of-FMV-or-exercise-price repurchase price for Cause terminations as off-market or confiscatory.
The deliverable proposes an alternative Cause-termination repurchase price that ensures the holder recoups at least the exercise price paid.
The repurchase provision exempts Tier 1 participants Dr. Chandrasekaran, Sorokin, and Dr. Osei from the repurchase right after a stated minimum tenure.
The option pool or allocation provision provides one fallback position if the investor rejects the initial compromise.
The option pool or allocation provision provides one fallback position if the founders reject the initial compromise.
The CIC acceleration provision provides one fallback position if the investor rejects the initial compromise.
The CIC acceleration provision provides one fallback position if the founders reject the initial compromise.
The PTEP provision provides one fallback position if the investor rejects the initial compromise.
The PTEP provision provides one fallback position if the founders reject the initial compromise.
The clawback or repurchase provision provides one fallback position if the investor rejects the initial compromise.
The clawback or repurchase provision provides one fallback position if the founders reject the initial compromise.
The fallback ladders identify the investor’s hard cap of 13.75% of fully diluted shares for the pool.
The fallback ladders identify the founders’ hard floor of 120 days for non-Cause PTEP.
The fallback ladders identify the founders’ hard floor that repurchase may not be below the exercise price.
The fallback ladders identify the investor’s requirement to retain repurchase for Cause terminations.
The stated maximum total pool, counting the initial reserve, maximum rollover, and maximum cumulative evergreen accrual, does not exceed 2,200,000 shares or 13.75% of 16,000,000 fully diluted shares.
The deliverable provides proposed contractual clause language for the option pool size and allocation provision that is suitable for insertion into the Plan.
The deliverable provides proposed contractual clause language for the Change of Control acceleration provision, including the tiered structure, suitable for insertion into the Plan.
The deliverable provides proposed contractual clause language for the post-termination exercise period provision suitable for insertion into the Plan.
The deliverable provides proposed contractual clause language for the clawback or repurchase rights provision suitable for insertion into the Plan.
Each of the four compromise provisions has a negotiation rationale explaining why its proposed position is fair and how it splits the gap between the parties.
Each of the four compromise provisions has a rationale citing supporting market data, such as the Aldridge Lydon market study.
The deliverable references and reconciles the 2020 Stock Option Plan as a baseline or precedent.
The deliverable discusses the 2020 Plan’s 90-day FMV repurchase right, which was never exercised.
The deliverable discusses the 2020 Plan’s single-trigger Change of Control acceleration for all holders.
The deliverable addresses employee option holders’ illiquidity hardship from a short PTEP.
The deliverable addresses the $8.40-per-share exercise cost for employee option holders.
The deliverable addresses employee option holders’ uncertainty under pure double-trigger Change of Control acceleration.
The deliverable incorporates a tenure-based PTEP concept.
The deliverable calculates the investor’s proposed dilution as $28,800,000 (2,400,000 × $12.00).
The deliverable calculates the founders’ new pool as $15,360,000 (1,280,000 × $12.00).
The deliverable calculates the founders’ total pool including rollover as 1,605,000 shares.
The deliverable calculates the dilution delta as $9,540,000 ((2,400,000 − 1,605,000) × $12.00).
The deliverable references or respects a compromise date of approximately June 18, 2025.
The deliverable references or respects a Board meeting target of July 15, 2025.
The deliverable references or respects a Series C closing target of August 1, 2025.
The compromise specifies Delaware law as the governing law for the Plan.
The compromise specifies AAA arbitration seated in Wilmington, Delaware for disputes.
The deliverable includes a summary comparison table covering the option pool, CIC acceleration, PTEP, and clawback or repurchase provisions.
For each of the four provisions, the table shows the investor’s original position, the founders’ original position, the compromise position, and the approximate concession split or balance.
